summary: NAT64/DNS64 translation of artifact hostnames breaks TLS SNI causing model artifact downloads to fail on private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer's Private deployment nodes fail to download model artifacts during provisioning. Control-plane and runtime log repeated TLS handshake failures showing certificate name mismatch. Customer runs a dual-stack VPC with DNS64/NAT64 enabled for IPv6-only worker subnets.

Impact:
- New workers fail to provision (stuck in 'model-pull' phase).
- Ingest and inference traffic on affected hosts intermittently falls back and triggers restarts; customers report degraded availability for pinned models.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-controlled VPC) in us-west-2
- Dual-stack VPC with customer-managed DNS64/NAT64 appliance
- Model artifacts hosted on redwood-artifacts.prod.redwood.internal (served by our artifact CDN TLS endpoint)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Bring up a worker in an IPv6-only subnet using the customer's VPC resolver (DNS64 enabled).
2) Start the redwood runtime that attempts to fetch artifacts from redwood-artifacts.prod.redwood.internal.
3) Observe runtime logs and TLS handshake failures.

Observed behavior:
- System resolves redwood-artifacts.prod.redwood.internal to an AAAA via DNS64 (synthesized).
- TLS client uses SNI equal to the resolved IPv6 literal (synthesized) or the resolver returns AAAA-only, causing the outgoing TLS handshake to not include the expected hostname and server responds with cert for artifact host; client interprets this as CN mismatch and terminates the connection.
- Logs show: "tls: handshake failure: x509: certificate is valid for redwood-artifacts.prod.redwood.internal, not [2001:db8::abcd]"

Expected behavior:
- Client should present correct SNI (artifact host) or resolver should provide A record so connection goes over IPv4 path without SNI mismatch. Artifacts should download successfully.

Attachments:
- Excerpts from runtime logs (see investigation_notes)
- Packet capture provided by customer (sftp link in comments)

investigation_notes:
Observations from logs and pcap:
- dig +short AAAA redwood-artifacts.prod.redwood.internal -> 2001:db8::abcd (synthesized by DNS64 appliance). dig +short A returns nothing from customer's resolver.
- Runtime TLS client uses SNI = 2001:db8::abcd in ClientHello in several traces (we suspect our runtime's getaddrinfo path returns numeric form when AAAA-only present).
- Server certificate CN/SAN contains redwood-artifacts.prod.redwood.internal (no IP SAN for the synthesized IPv6). TLS negotiation fails with x509: certificate is valid for redwood-artifacts.prod.redwood.internal, not [2001:db8::abcd].
- Packet capture shows IPv6 flow to appliance then NAT64 translating to IPv4 to our CDN edge; server returns certificate for hostname as expected. Client rejects because SNI did not match the cert name.
- Workaround test: adding an /etc/hosts entry pointing redwood-artifacts.prod.redwood.internal -> 54.210.12.34 (IPv4) forced the client to use IPv4 and TLS handshake succeeded.
Hypothesis:
- Customer DNS64 synthesizes AAAA only; runtime is resolving to numeric address and populating SNI with the numeric form rather than the original hostname. On AAAA-only resolution, SNI should still be set to the original hostname; failure stems from client behavior or glibc resolver variant.
Recommendations tried:
- /etc/hosts override (successful test).
- Creating VPC endpoint to keep artifact traffic on IPv4 (customer to test).
- Suggested customer to enable split-horizon so artifact host resolves to A record for their VPC subnets.
resolution:
Workaround and next steps:
- Short-term workaround: Customer added /etc/hosts mapping to an IPv4 artifact edge on test nodes which allowed provisioning to proceed.
- Medium-term remediation: Customer will create a VPC endpoint and/or configure split-DNS to return A records for redwood-artifacts.prod.redwood.internal from their resolver for worker subnets (planned this week).
- Redwood follow-up: INT-33045 created for engineering to add detection when resolver returns synthesized AAAA and to prefer original hostname as SNI or attempt IPv4 fallback before failing TLS.
- Follow-up actions assigned:
  - Customer: Implement VPC endpoint / split-DNS and validate in staging (owner: Pinebank infra).
  - Support: Provide runbook for network team (link shared in comments).
  - Eng (INT-33045): Evaluate runtime resolver/SNI behavior and implement robust fallback.
Status: Waiting on Customer (implementation in staging).
